steps.description: Identify the planner component responsible for generating run_command steps
steps.details: Examine the codebase to locate the specific module or function where run_command steps are generated. This will likely involve understanding the current logic that constructs these steps.

steps.description: Modify the planner to enforce executable shell commands
steps.details: Update the logic in the identified module to ensure that all run_command steps generate real, executable shell commands. Remove any logic that allows placeholders like 'test suite for planner'. Ensure that the commands are formatted to be directly runnable in a local environment.

steps.description: Implement validation logic for run_command steps
steps.details: Add a validation function that checks each run_command step to ensure it is a real, executable shell command. This function should reject any command that contains placeholders or cannot be executed in a local environment. Integrate this validation into the planner's workflow.

steps.description: Test the updated planner for compliance with new rules
steps.details: Run the test suite for the planner to ensure that all changes comply with the new rules. Specifically, verify that all run_command steps are executable and that the validation logic correctly identifies and rejects non-executable commands.

steps.description: Document changes made to the planner
steps.details: Create a new documentation file that outlines the changes made to the planner. Include details on the new enforcement of executable shell commands, the removal of placeholders, and the validation logic.
